product_offering.core_offering: Accertify provides a unified AI-powered risk decisioning platform that combines identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals to detect and prevent fraud, account takeover, returns abuse, and chargebacks for enterprise merchants across the full customer lifecycle — from account creation through post-purchase dispute resolution. The offering spans Account Protection, Fraud Detection, Returns and Abuse Protection, Payment Optimization (including 3DS), Chargeback Management, and a Payment Gateway, augmented by the Predictive Yes Platform, Passwordless Suite, and a consortium intelligence layer covering 10B+ annual transactions across hundreds of enterprise brands.
product_offering.differentiator: Accertify differentiates through its Predictive Yes Platform — a unified risk decisioning layer that connects identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle. Key differentiators include: (1) consortium data from 10B+ annual transactions across hundreds of enterprise brands, enabling 98% client data sharing; (2) multi-model orchestration spanning machine learning, graph networks, and sequential transformers rather than replacing older models; (3) industry-specific AI models calibrated to retail, travel, ticketing, iGaming, and financial services verticals; (4) account protection capabilities processing 1.6B+ events with 49.7% YoY growth; (5) passwordless authentication suite aligned with FIDO/WebAuthn standards.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Approves more legitimate transactions while reducing fraud losses; reduces manual review rates (up to 20% reduction documented); decreases fraud losses (62% reduction at Guitar Center, 80%+ at Sportsbet); reduces chargebacks (71% at Target Australia, 30%+ at Fnac Darty); enables frictionless customer journeys (99%+ frictionless acceptance rates); provides real-time decisioning at sub-100ms latency with proven peak performance of 2,708 TPS; prevents account takeover, bot attacks, coordinated login attacks (Attack State), and returns abuse; stops 30.7M+ fraud/abuse attempts worth $5.8B annually.
product_offering.problem_solved: Accertify solves the fundamental tension between fraud prevention and revenue growth for enterprise merchants: fraud teams must reduce fraud losses while not sacrificing approval rates on legitimate customers, and must do so at massive transaction scale in real time. The platform addresses coordinated login attacks, account takeover, payment fraud, returns abuse, chargebacks, bot attacks, synthetic identity fraud, and first-party misuse across the full customer lifecycle from account creation through post-purchase dispute resolution.

product_offering.product_overview: Accertify is a unified risk decisioning platform provider offering an integrated suite of fraud prevention, account protection, abuse prevention, payment optimization, chargeback management, and payment gateway solutions. The core portfolio includes the Predictive Yes Platform (enterprise fraud decisioning connecting identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals), Account Protection (device intelligence and behavior analytics for account takeover prevention), Fraud Detection (multi-layered ML-based prevention), Returns and Abuse Protection (wardrobing and return fraud detection), Payment Optimization (including 3DS optimization), Chargeback Management, and the Payment Gateway. Additional modules include Attack State Intelligence (coordinated login attack detection) and Passwordless Suite (FIDO2-compliant authentication). The platform processes over 10 billion transactions annually worth $1.25 trillion in commerce, with 98% of clients sharing anonymized fraud intelligence through a consortium approach across retail, travel, ticketing, and other sectors.

product_and_service.description: Enterprise fraud decisioning technology that connects identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle from account creation through post-purchase. Processes over 10 billion transactions and $1.25 trillion in commerce annually with a consortium approach where 98% of clients share anonymized fraud intelligence.
product_and_service.name: Predictive Yes Platform

product_and_service.description: Solution that uses sophisticated device technology and advanced user behavior analytics to identify and protect against fraudulent account openings, multi-accounting abuse, and account takeover attacks. Provides real-time end-to-end insights from the moment a customer lands on a digital doorstep, distinguishing authentic visitors from potential threats.
product_and_service.name: Account Protection

product_and_service.description: Multi-layered fraud prevention platform built on advanced machine learning, device intelligence, and user behavior analytics. Built on four core principles: Predict (ML with rich community data), Prevent (standard API with day-one risk decisioning), Protect (ML-driven risk strategies), and People (human intelligence and deep domain expertise).
product_and_service.name: Fraud Detection

product_and_service.description: Solution that monitors, measures, and curbs return abuse while designing return policies that protect margins without punishing good customers. Detects wardrobing, return swapping, falsifying delivery, and shipping label fraud. Collects return data via specialized API tracking customer return activity across email, account IDs, phone numbers, geolocations, shipping addresses, and payment methods.
product_and_service.name: Returns and Abuse Protection

product_and_service.description: Solution focused on optimizing payment performance including 3D Secure (3DS) implementation, authentication strategies, and authorization rate improvement. Helps merchants transform 3DS from a conversion killer into a strategic performance lever through better data sharing and risk scoring.
product_and_service.name: Payment Optimization

product_and_service.description: Solution for managing chargebacks and disputes integrated into the unified platform, helping merchants reduce chargeback rates and streamline dispute resolution workflows.
product_and_service.name: Chargeback Management

product_and_service.description: Payment gateway solution integrated into the unified risk decisioning platform, enabling merchants to process payments while maintaining fraud protection across the transaction lifecycle.
product_and_service.name: Payment Gateway

product_and_service.description: Passwordless authentication solution offering Magic Links (one-tap login via secure email link) and Passkeys (biometric/PIN-based authentication per FIDO2 standards). Reduces password-based risks, phishing, and credential theft while maintaining friction-free transactions.
product_and_service.name: Passwordless Suite

Launched the Predictive Yes Platform, a unified risk decisioning technology connecting identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle, backed by $1.25T in annual commerce data.
Appointed Greg Dukat as CEO alongside CSO Trey McCall, CMO Maryling Yu, MD EMEA Emma Lindley, and Global HR Head Sara Schroeder to lead next-phase growth.

Launched Attack State Intelligence, a new capability within Account Protection designed to detect and respond to coordinated login attacks, credential stuffing, and account takeover attempts in real time.

Entered a referral partnership with RegTech Solutions Pty Ltd to extend account protection capabilities into Australia's financial services sector, including superannuation, wealth, and investment platforms.

expansion_highlight.description: RegTech Solutions referral partnership (announced 2025-11-04) opens the Australian financial services vertical — superannuation, wealth managers, investment platforms — a regulated sector with high-value fraud prevention budgets. Strategic intent: leverage partnership GTM to enter a vertical without building direct sales infrastructure.

Registered office presence across UK, Spain, Australia, Mexico, and India, plus active participation in regional industry events (MRC Melbourne 2026, FraudCon 2026 Sydney, MAG Payments Summit London), signals deliberate EMEA and APAC expansion following the 2024 Accel-KKR carve-out.

Launch of the Predictive Yes Platform (May 2026) and Attack State Intelligence (March 2026), plus the Passwordless Suite (April 2025) and Returns and Abuse Protection, represents platform surface expansion into adjacent fraud domains — from payment fraud into account protection, authentication, and returns abuse — increasing wallet share per customer.

Executive team expansion (CSO, CMO, MD EMEA, Global HR Head) plus appointment of Carleigh Jaques (former Visa SVP Risk & Identity) to the board in 2026 indicates deliberate go-to-market buildout — likely scaling sales capacity to capture the 24% YoY client growth into accelerated enterprise wins.

Salesforce Commerce Cloud integration via AppExchange Marketplace (purpose-built, tested integration) signals an indirect-channel/partnership GTM buildout to accelerate merchant onboarding in the Salesforce commerce ecosystem — a non-trivial distribution expansion beyond direct field sales.

Addition of Marketplaces as an industry vertical on the website (post-2024) plus explicit multi-vendor/seller-fraud use cases signals productization for two-sided marketplace platforms — a customer segment with distinct fraud economics from single-sided retail.

company_assessment.market_position: Accertify is a privately held, PE-backed (Accel-KKR, since 2024 carve-out from American Express) enterprise fraud prevention and risk management platform founded in 2007, headquartered in Itasca, Illinois, with operations across North America, EMEA, APAC, and LATAM and 501–1,000 employees. The company positions itself as a unified lifecycle risk decisioning provider serving some of the world's largest brands (including United Airlines, Walmart, Marks & Spencer, Sportsbet, Target Australia, and Fnac Darty), processing more than 10 billion transactions and protecting roughly $5.8 billion in attempted fraud annually. Its differentiated go-to-market is built around a consortium data model in which 98% of clients contribute anonymized fraud intelligence, giving Accertify a cross-merchant signal advantage that compounds as its client base grows 24% year over year.

strengths.details: With 98% of clients already contributing fraud intelligence and the client base expanding 24% YoY, each new enterprise brand materially strengthens detection accuracy for the entire network. As the consortium grows, marginal fraud detection improvement per new client accelerates, raising switching costs and supporting both win-rates and pricing power against incumbents like Visa and Mastercard.
strengths.headline: Consortium network effect compounds with 24% YoY client growth

strengths.details: Account Protection events grew 49.7% YoY to 1.63 billion, while Attack State and the Passwordless Suite expand the platform beyond transaction fraud into login, account takeover, and authentication. This positions Accertify to capture a share of the broader identity-and-access fraud and authentication market, layering additional ARR on top of the existing fraud-detection footprint.
strengths.headline: Account Protection platform opens new $5B+ adjacent TAM

strengths.details: As autonomous shopping agents erode traditional device and behavioral signals, smaller point solutions built on legacy signal stacks will lose accuracy. Accertify's multi-model orchestration (ML, graph networks, sequential transformers) and 10B+ transaction dataset give it a defensible position to develop agent-aware risk models and win business displaced from weaker vendors.
strengths.headline: Agentic AI disruption favors sophisticated incumbent platforms

strengths.details: The RegTech Solutions partnership in Australia signals a push into financial services (superannuation, wealth, investment platforms), and the company maintains offices in the UK, Spain, Australia, with operations spanning India and Mexico. Each new vertical and region extends the consortium's data diversity, which directly improves model performance across the existing client base.
strengths.headline: Financial services and EMEA expansion drive geographic and vertical diversification

strengths.details: Following the 2024 Accel-KKR carve-out, Accertify rebuilt leadership with operators from Visa (board), and executives recruited from outside the prior AmEx structure. Combined with PE capital and aggressive event/conference marketing (MRC Vegas, London, Melbourne, FraudCon), this points to an accelerated land-and-expand motion in 2026–2027.
strengths.headline: PE-backed commercial intensity and fresh executive team accelerate market share gain

weakness.details: Visa and Mastercard continue embedding risk decisioning (e.g., Visa Risk Manager, Mastercard Decision Intelligence) directly into card-network rails, often at no incremental cost to merchants. As these offerings mature, Accertify faces structural pricing pressure and renewal erosion, particularly among merchants who view fraud as a commodity feature rather than a specialized capability.
weakness.headline: Card network incumbents bundle fraud and squeeze margins

weakness.details: Conrad Kennington (Accertify's VP of AI/ML) has publicly acknowledged that autonomous agents eliminate traditional browser, device, and behavioral signals. If agent-driven traffic scales rapidly, the consortium's historical signal value could degrade, forcing costly model re-architecture and creating a window of lower detection accuracy that competitors can exploit.
weakness.headline: Agentic commerce erodes core signal-based moat

weakness.details: Accel-KKR's typical 3–5 year hold window means an exit transaction is likely within the next 1–3 years. This could pressure Accertify to prioritize short-term ARR growth over product depth, accept a discounted strategic sale that undervalues the platform, or face a down-round financing if public-market comparables (e.g., Riskified's share-price trajectory) weaken.
weakness.headline: PE exit timing may force premature strategic decisions

weakness.details: Anchored customer logos include multiple global airlines (United, JetBlue, Southwest, Ryanair, Volaris, WestJet) and discretionary retail brands. A travel downturn, pandemic-style disruption, or retail squeeze would simultaneously reduce transaction volume and increase fraud-loss pressure, compressing revenue and customer ROI in tandem.
weakness.headline: Concentration in airlines and discretionary retail exposes to cyclical shocks

weakness.details: Riskified, Sift, and Forter continue to raise capital and pour investment into AI-driven fraud models. Although Accertify's consortium dataset is a structural advantage, a sustained R&D spend gap from venture-backed competitors could narrow product differentiation over time, particularly in newer attack surfaces like agentic commerce.
weakness.headline: Venture-backed competitors outpace innovation spend

competitive_moat.details: Consortium data from 10B+ annual transactions and $1.25T in commerce across hundreds of enterprise brands, with 98% of clients sharing anonymized fraud signals — a scale of cross-merchant intelligence that competitors without comparable installed bases cannot replicate quickly.

Consortium model creates compounding intelligence value: as the client base grows (24% YoY), each merchant benefits from fraud signals observed across the broader network, creating a self-reinforcing moat that strengthens with scale.

Multi-product platform spanning account protection, fraud detection, returns abuse, payment optimization, 3DS, chargeback management, and passwordless authentication — integrated into merchant workflows with API-level customization, creating significant operational switching friction.

Proprietary multi-model orchestration architecture combining rules engines, supervised ML, graph networks, and sequential transformers, plus industry-specific models calibrated to retail, travel, ticketing, iGaming, and financial services verticals.

19-year operating history with marquee enterprise logos (Walmart, United Airlines, Marks & Spencer, Ticketmaster, DraftKings, Target Australia) and deep MRC/industry association positioning provides channel and reference-customer advantages in enterprise sales cycles.

Leadership team includes a dedicated VP of AI/ML (Conrad Kennington), Director of Fraud & Account Protection (Stuart Mann) re-elected to MRC Global Board, and recently appointed board member Carleigh Jaques (former Visa SVP Risk & Identity) — concentrated domain expertise in payments risk.

key_risks.details: Accertify competes against large network incumbents (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) integrating fraud into card rails and well-funded venture-backed competitors (Sift, Riskified, Forter, Signifyd, Stripe Radar). Network incumbents can bundle fraud at marginal cost, pressuring standalone pricing and renewal economics.
key_risks.headline: Highly competitive market with deep-pocketed network incumbents and well-funded pure-plays

key_risks.details: Accertify sells exclusively through direct enterprise field sales targeting large global merchants with a consultative 'Request a Demo' motion. This produces long sales cycles, heavy S&M spend, and lumpier revenue recognition compared to self-serve or channel-led competitors.
key_risks.headline: Enterprise sales motion creates long cycles and high customer acquisition costs

key_risks.details: Customer logo concentration in airlines (United, JetBlue, Southwest, Ryanair, Volaris, WestJet) and retail (Walmart, Target Australia, Marks & Spencer) ties revenue to discretionary travel and consumer spending cycles, which have historically been disrupted by macro events.
key_risks.headline: Sector concentration in travel and retail exposes revenue to cyclical shocks

key_risks.details: Accel-KKR's typical 3–5 year PE hold cycle creates implicit pressure for growth-at-all-costs investment, an exit event (sale, secondary buyout, or IPO), and aggressive commercial metrics. This can divert focus from product depth or create churn risk during ownership transitions.
key_risks.headline: PE ownership horizon creates exit pressure and potential strategic constraints

key_risks.details: Accertify's own VP of AI/ML publicly noted that autonomous shopping agents eliminate traditional fraud signals such as browser data and device signals. As agentic commerce grows, the company's behavioral and device intelligence moat could erode faster than new agent-aware models can be developed.
key_risks.headline: Emerging AI-agent commerce threatens core signal architecture

key_risks.details: Accertify does not disclose pricing tiers, revenue, ARR, or margin data publicly. While this is normal for a PE-backed private company, it limits third-party diligence and benchmarking against public peers such as Riskified.
key_risks.headline: Limited pricing transparency and no public financial disclosures

key_highlights.details: The Predictive Yes Platform leverages data from over 10 billion transactions and $1.25 trillion in commerce processed annually. 98% of Accertify clients share anonymized fraud intelligence across hundreds of enterprise brands, creating a self-reinforcing data moat that smaller competitors cannot easily replicate.
key_highlights.headline: Massive consortium data scale of 10B+ transactions and $1.25T commerce processed annually

key_highlights.details: Customer results include Sportsbet cutting fraud losses by 80%+ YoY and chargebacks by 82%+, Target Australia reducing chargebacks by 71% while maintaining 99% frictionless journeys, Guitar Center decreasing fraud losses 62% and increasing prevented fraud 106% YoY, and United Airlines raising win rate by 40%+. Customer logos include Walmart, United Airlines, Marks & Spencer, Ticketmaster, DraftKings, and JetBlue.
key_highlights.headline: Demonstrated enterprise-grade outcomes with marquee global brands

key_highlights.details: Accertify's client base expanded 24% year over year in 2025, indicating accelerating enterprise adoption of its unified risk decisioning platform and a meaningful shift toward identity-plus-fraud consolidation in the merchant market.
key_highlights.headline: Strong top-of-funnel momentum with 24% YoY client base growth

key_highlights.details: Account Protection events grew 49.7% year over year to 1.63 billion events spanning logins, account changes, session behavior, and bot activity. This signals significant upsell traction beyond core transaction fraud detection into the full customer lifecycle.
key_highlights.headline: Account Protection product scaling rapidly at 49.7% YoY event growth

key_highlights.details: Cyber Week 2025 handled 107 million transactions, $12.9 billion in commerce, and a peak of 2,708 transactions per second. This level of throughput and reliability under peak holiday load is a key qualification for enterprise merchants evaluating fraud vendors.
key_highlights.headline: Proven scale with proven technical performance

key_highlights.details: Accertify was carved out from American Express by Accel-KKR in 2024, with new executive leadership including CEO Greg Dukat, CSO Trey McCall, and CMO Maryling Yu added to drive an aggressive growth phase. Board member Carleigh Jaques (formerly SVP at Visa) adds senior industry credibility.
key_highlights.headline: Strategic PE sponsorship by Accel-KKR provides growth capital and operating expertise

key_highlights.details: Industry-specific machine learning models are calibrated for retail, travel, ticketing, iGaming, and financial services, embedding vertical-native signals (e.g., impossible route detection for airlines, deposit cycling for iGaming) that generic cross-industry models cannot match.
key_highlights.headline: Vertical-specialized AI models create differentiation versus horizontal fraud vendors
